gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 has a single solar input whose current limit drops to 8.2 A whenever the array works below 29 V. If two panels on that one input run below 29 V, the station takes about 230 W at most (28 V × 8.2 A), not its rated 600 W. The EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus gives each of the two panels its own 500 W MPPT input.
standout_why: ChatGPT cited the Anker a1765 page. That page prints 'MPPT: 11-28v⎓8.2A; 29V-60V⎓14.5A (600W Max)', but only inside a spec table and with no explanation. ChatGPT's answer then repeated '600W … 1.8 hours' with no condition attached. The cited EcoFlow pages (REI manual, us.ecoflow.com) and solargenreview cover only the DELTA 3 Plus. I could not open REI (403) or solargenreview (429), so I read EcoFlow's own FAQ and series page in their place. Neither the cited pages nor ChatGPT's answer turns Anker's voltage bands into what the shopper needs to know: how two panels must be wired to reach 600 W, and what happens if they aren't. That makes the finding new and useful. It is not a 3 because the raw numbers already appear on one cited page. I did not open the uncited explainers (stormwatts, voltandvalley, wattratings), so I can't rule out that one of them makes the general point about voltage.
decides: Confirms the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus as the pick for two panels. It has two separate PV inputs ('DELTA 3 Plus has 2 inputs', '500W MPPT × 2', EcoFlow), so each panel works within its own 11–60 V, 15 A, 500 W limit and no series or parallel wiring is needed. The Anker C1000 Gen 2, ChatGPT's runner-up, puts both panels on one input. It reaches its 600 W ceiling only if that array works at about 41 V or more (600 W ÷ 14.5 A) while staying at or under 60 V open-circuit. A pair of panels working below 29 V is limited to roughly 230 W, which stretches the advertised 1.8 h refill to about 4.5 h or more (1,024 Wh ÷ 230 W, before losses). The page should tell C1000 Gen 2 buyers to check their panels' working voltage (Vmp) and combined open-circuit voltage (Voc) before trusting the 1.8 h figure.

findings.label: Solar (MPPT) input current limit by voltage band
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen2 - Anker SOLIX US
findings.note: Verbatim from the INPUT table: '11-28v⎓8.2A; 29V-60V⎓14.5A (600W Max)'. The same bands are on https://www.ankersolix.com/products/c1000-gen2, also read 2026-11-15. Arithmetic: the most the station can take below 29 V is 28 V × 8.2 A ≈ 230 W. To reach 600 W at the 14.5 A limit, the array must work at 600 ÷ 14.5 ≈ 41.4 V or more.

findings.label: EcoFlow's rule for combining panels on one input
findings.value: Open-circuit voltage must fall within the input's voltage range, current must not exceed the input maximum, and total power must not exceed the input maximum; example limits 11–60 V, 15 A, 500 W
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus | EcoFlow Product FAQs | EcoFlow US
findings.note: The worked example uses the DELTA 3's single input (11–60 V, 15 A, 500 W). Two 400 W panels: in series about 957 W, which is over 500 W; in parallel about 25.8 A, which is over 15 A. Either way, two large panels on one 500 W input are capped. This is why the DELTA 3 Plus's second input matters.
